Interactions Since epoprostenol is a potent vasodilator and inhibitor of platelet aggregation, care should be taken in patients receiving other vasodilators or anticoagulants. Epo- prostenol may slightly increase serum concentrations of digoxin, and may reduce the thrombolytic effect of alteplase by increasing its hepatic clearance. The hypo- tensive effects of epoprostenol may be exacerbated by using acetate in dialysis fluids. Anticoagulants. The incidence of bleeding complications was examined in a retrospective review1 of 31 patients with primary pulmonary hypertension who had been treated with continuous intravenous epoprostenol and oral warfarin.
